title: Chinese Claypot Rice
description: A pot of ginger-garlic rice with mushrooms and your choice of chicken, pork, beef or lean pork mince.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of chicken claypot rice in a rustic clay pot, with chicken, Chinese sausage and spring onions.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · traditional chicken and sausage variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Dinner and lunch for both of us. Pick whichever meat we have, and don’t worry if it’s a little less salty: the lime helps the flavour too, and we can add soy sauce at the table.
equipment: Large pot with a close-fitting lid
Bowl or sieve for washing rice
Containers for the next day’s lunches
advancePrep: Check the freezer for ginger-garlic blocks. For the original four-portion batch, 4 blocks replace the head of garlic and 50 g of ginger.
importantNotes: Four portions: dinner for both of us and two lunches for tomorrow. For our batch, use 600–800 g of whichever one meat you choose. Prep time is an estimate. Don’t open the lid during the final 10-minute rest.

groups.title: For the meat, mushrooms and rice

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.note: Use 600–800 g for our four-portion batch, diced small. Or use the same range of sliced pork loin, thinly sliced beef steak or 5% lean pork mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: Peel and chop finely. Or replace this and the ginger with 4 ginger-garlic blocks for our batch.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: Peel and chop finely; omit if using the ginger-garlic blocks.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: Brown or red, whichever is available; chop.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.note: Wash in cold water three times if possible, then drain.

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.note: To drizzle over the finished rice.

ingredients.name: Extra soy sauce
ingredients.note: Add at the table only if wanted.

steps.title: Prepare the meat and aromatics
steps.description: Pick whichever meat we’re using, Jack: small diced chicken, sliced pork loin, thin beef steaks or 5% lean pork mince. Slice the mushrooms. Check for ginger-garlic blocks in the freezer, or peel and finely chop the garlic and ginger. Chop whichever onion we have and boil the measured water.

steps.title: Cook the meat, garlic, ginger and onion
steps.description: Put the garlic, ginger, onion and meat in the pot. Cook on medium for 10 minutes, squishing everything around, until the onion softens and the meat changes colour. If you’re using mince, break up the clumps as you go.
steps.doneness: Soft onion; chicken or pork pale on the outside, or beef and mince losing their raw colour.
steps.warning: The initial colour change does not prove the meat is cooked through; it continues cooking in the next stages.

steps.title: Add the mushrooms
steps.description: Add the mushrooms and squish them around for 2 minutes, until they start letting out some water.

steps.title: Add the turmeric and stock
steps.description: Add the turmeric, boiled water, chicken stock cubes and dark soy. Mix it around, get it bubbling and leave it to cook for 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Wash and drain the rice while the pot bubbles.

steps.title: Wash the rice while the pot cooks
steps.description: While the pot bubbles, wash the rice in cold water three times if you can. We’re getting the extra starch out so it stays more separate. Drain it and have it ready for when the 20 minutes are up.

steps.title: Add the rice and pepper
steps.description: Once the 20 minutes are up, add the washed, drained rice and crushed black pepper, then mix everything around.

steps.title: Cook the rice with the lid on
steps.description: Cover it and cook for 15 minutes. Keep it gently bubbling on medium-low heat.

steps.title: Rest without opening the lid
steps.description: Turn off the stove, but don’t open the lid yet. Give the rice another 10 minutes to sit in the steam.
steps.doneness: Rice rested with the steam kept inside.

steps.title: Serve with lime and sesame oil
steps.description: Open the lid and check that the rice and meat are cooked. Serve our dinner straight away with lime wedges and sesame oil. If it needs more salt, add a little extra soy sauce to your plate. Try the lime too—it brightens the flavour, so less salt is fine. Put our lunch portions aside to cool promptly.
steps.doneness: Cooked rice and fully cooked meat.
steps.tip: Lime also brightens the flavour, so a little less salt is fine.
steps.warning: If using chicken or mince, a thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. If the meat is not cooked through, continue cooking before serving.

substitutions.title: Choose your meat
substitutions.text: For the original four-portion batch, use 600–800 g of small diced chicken, sliced pork loin steaks, thinly sliced beef steak or 5% lean pork mince. Use one meat option, not all four.

substitutions.title: Freezer ginger-garlic blocks
substitutions.text: Use 4 blocks for the original batch instead of the head of garlic and 50 g ginger.

substitutions.title: Onion
substitutions.text: Use a brown or red onion, whichever is available.

troubleshooting.title: Want a little more flavour?
troubleshooting.text: Try the lime wedges and sesame oil, then add extra soy sauce at the table if wanted.

troubleshooting.title: Keeping the rice separate
troubleshooting.text: Wash it three times if possible, drain it, and keep the lid on during the final rest.

storage: Divide the two lunch portions into small containers and cool quickly, ideally within 1 hour. Refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.
reheating: Reheat a lunch portion once until steaming hot throughout. Stir or turn it when microwaving to avoid cold pockets.
foodSafety: Meat must be cooked through before serving. A thermometer check for chicken and mince is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Keep utensils used for raw meat away from the finished rice.
servingSuggestion: Dinner for both of us, plus two lunch portions. Serve with lime wedges, sesame oil and extra soy sauce if wanted.
